terms.gloss: I’ll catch up with you in a moment!
evidence: Ter. Hec. 358: cōnsequar jam tē, mea māter
terms.comment: In Terence a son’s promise to follow his mother indoors at once; in the chasing game the same words are a playful threat, for cōnsequor is to follow someone and catch up (Lewis & Short: “to reach, overtake, come up with”). We have found no ancient chasing call. To threaten a grab instead, Jam tē prehendam!: prehendō, to catch hold of (Lewis & Short), with jam and the future, as in Plautus’s Jam ego hīc erō (Men. 225).

phrases.latin: Ī sōdēs intrō; cōnsequar jam tē, mea māter.
phrases.english: Go on in, please; I’ll be right behind you, Mother.

sources: Lewis & Short: consequor · Lewis & Short: prehendo
Terence and Plautus from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-terentius, loci-plautus).
